title: RADIO AM/FM-RECEIVER ASM & MOUNTING
summary: RPO U69 AM/FM radio receiver in the center of the instrument panel. The receiver's control shafts come through the dash and are held by shaft nuts (45-60 LBS IN), with spacer, washers and the inner/outer knobs; the rear of the receiver is braced by a bracket nutted to a stud on the receiver (20-30 LBS IN) and screwed into a U-nut (40-60 LBS IN). A convector (FM converter) assembly is screwed up under the dash (25-35 LBS IN) and plugs into the receiver; the sheet also gives the antenna trimmer peaking procedure.

parts.name: CONVECTOR ASM.
parts.name_expanded: Convector assembly (as printed) – unit mounted under the dash, with connector to receiver

fastening.to: underside of the instrument panel (upper dash, RH of receiver)
fastening.note: Screw [2] goes up through the mounting tab of convector assembly [1] into the dash.

Nuts [7] thread onto the receiver's control shaft bushings from the front of the dash, clamping the receiver [9]. Stack-up on each shaft, front of dash outward: nut [7], (RH side: spacer [6]), washer [5], knob [8], knob [3]. Antenna trimmer screw is beside the RH shaft.
View A: nut [12] goes on a stud on the side/rear of receiver [9] (stud is part of the receiver, no separate callout) and holds the upper slot of bracket [13].

fastening.to: instrument panel support/reinforcement below the receiver
fastening.note: View A: screw [11] goes through the lower hole of bracket [13] into U-nut [10] clipped on the dash support tab.
View A: connector (part of [1]) plugs into the back of the receiver.

notes: Peaking the antenna trimmer: (1) set antenna mast height to 31.00 ± 1.00 in; (2) volume knob to maximum; (3) tune to a station at or near 1400 KC on the AM scale; (4) turn the antenna trimmer screw (about ±2° of rotation) until volume is greatest; (5) turn receiver off.
